en.display_text:
Consider the following statements offering an integrated analysis of Din-i-Ilahi's philosophical foundations, failure, and long-term reversal:

1. Sulh-i-Kul operated as the philosophical ideal underpinning Akbar's entire syncretic program, while Din-i-Ilahi was its institutional expression in the specific form of a court devotional order.
2. Din-i-Ilahi failed primarily because it was actively persecuted by Jahangir, who imposed legal penalties on those who had joined the order.
3. The ulema's issuance of an apostasy fatwa against Akbar during the 1580-81 rebellion and the survival of Din-i-Ilahi until Akbar's death in 1605 together suggest that the order's failure was internal rather than the result of external religious opposition.
4. The restoration of jizya by Aurangzeb in 1679 is the most often cited single-policy marker indicating the degree to which Akbar's religious liberalism was subsequently reversed within the Mughal dynasty.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 and 3 only
(b) 1, 3 and 4 only
(c) 2, 3 and 4 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3 only

statement_analysis.statement: Sulh-i-Kul operated as the philosophical ideal underpinning Akbar's entire syncretic program, while Din-i-Ilahi was its institutional expression in the specific form of a court devotional order.
statement_analysis.reason: This accurately describes the hierarchical relationship: Sulh-i-Kul as the broader philosophical principle and Din-i-Ilahi as the specific institutional form it took within the court.

statement_analysis.statement: Din-i-Ilahi failed primarily because it was actively persecuted by Jahangir, who imposed legal penalties on those who had joined the order.
statement_analysis.reason: Din-i-Ilahi did not fail due to active persecution — Jahangir simply did not continue it. The failure was structural: no institutional infrastructure, no successor leadership, complete dependence on Akbar's personal charisma.

statement_analysis.statement: The ulema's issuance of an apostasy fatwa against Akbar during the 1580-81 rebellion and the survival of Din-i-Ilahi until Akbar's death in 1605 together suggest that the order's failure was internal rather than the result of external religious opposition.
statement_analysis.reason: If external religious opposition (the 1580-81 fatwa) had been the primary cause of failure, Din-i-Ilahi would have collapsed by the early 1580s — but it survived until 1605. Its collapse upon Akbar's death confirms the structural/internal explanation.

statement_analysis.statement: The restoration of jizya by Aurangzeb in 1679 is the most often cited single-policy marker indicating the degree to which Akbar's religious liberalism was subsequently reversed within the Mughal dynasty.
statement_analysis.reason: Aurangzeb's 1679 jizya re-imposition — 115 years after Akbar's 1564 abolition — is consistently cited by historians as the emblematic reversal of Akbari religious policy.

en.strong_distractor: d — Option d ('1, 2 and 3 only') is deceptive because students who know Statement 4 sounds like a textbook fact may accept all four, or students who correctly eliminate Statement 2 may incorrectly also eliminate Statement 4 from uncertainty.
elimination_logic: Verify Statement 1: Sulh-i-Kul as philosophical base, Din-i-Ilahi as institutional expression — correct and analytically precise.
Examine Statement 2: 'actively persecuted by Jahangir' with 'legal penalties' — fabricated; Jahangir simply did not continue Din-i-Ilahi; no persecution occurred; Statement 2 is incorrect.

Verify Statement 3: The logical argument — fatwa in 1580-81 did not kill Din-i-Ilahi, but Akbar's death in 1605 did — confirms internal/structural failure rather than external opposition; Statement 3 is correct.
Verify Statement 4: Aurangzeb 1679 jizya re-imposition as prime marker of reversal — correct and standard in historiography.
Statements 1, 3, and 4 correct; Statement 2 incorrect → answer is (b) 1, 3 and 4 only.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 introduces a plausible-fabrication: the claim that Jahangir 'imposed legal penalties' on former Din-i-Ilahi members sounds like it could be true given Jahangir's more orthodox stance. Students who correctly know Jahangir was less tolerant than Akbar may extend this into assuming active persecution. In fact, Jahangir's approach was simply to not continue Din-i-Ilahi — there is no documented legal prosecution of former members.
en.final_explanation:
This integrative question draws together the major analytical themes of the topic — the nature of Din-i-Ilahi, its failure, the ulema's opposition, and the long-term reversal of Akbar's policies.

• Statement 1 — Correct: The Sulh-i-Kul/Din-i-Ilahi relationship is a foundational distinction. Sulh-i-Kul was the cosmic-philosophical ideal; Din-i-Ilahi was its institutionalized court-level expression with rituals, membership, and discipleship.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: Jahangir did not impose legal penalties on Din-i-Ilahi members. The order dissolved through institutional entropy — no charismatic murshid to hold it together, no successor, no infrastructure. 'Active persecution' is a fabrication.
• Statement 3 — Correct: The logic here is important. If external opposition (1580-81 fatwa) had destroyed Din-i-Ilahi, it would not have survived until 1605. Its survival through external opposition but collapse upon Akbar's death clinches the structural/internal failure explanation.
• Statement 4 — Correct: Aurangzeb's 1679 jizya re-imposition is the single sharpest policy reversal of Akbar's legacy — a 115-year gap closing with a symbolic return to pre-Akbari practice.

Value Addition:
• The logical argument in Statement 3 (surviving external opposition → internal failure explanation) is a model for analytical Prelims reasoning.
• For GS1 mains: structure your Din-i-Ilahi failure answer around three causes — structural weakness, narrow social base, personal charisma dependency.
• Akbar's broader legacy (jizya abolition, Rajput integration, composite culture) outlasted Din-i-Ilahi itself — the order was the most visible but least durable part of his syncretic project.

कथन 1, 3, और 4 सही; कथन 2 गलत → उत्तर है (b) केवल 1, 3 और 4।
hi.upsc_trap_explanation: कथन 2 एक संभावित निर्मित तथ्य प्रस्तुत करता है: यह दावा कि Jahangir ने पूर्व Din-i-Ilahi सदस्यों पर 'कानूनी दंड' लगाए, यह सुनने में सच लग सकता है क्योंकि Jahangir का रुख Akbar से अधिक रूढ़िवादी था। जो छात्र जानते हैं कि Jahangir कम सहिष्णु था, वे इसे सक्रिय उत्पीड़न मान सकते हैं। वास्तव में, Jahangir ने बस Din-i-Ilahi को जारी नहीं रखा — पूर्व सदस्यों के खिलाफ कोई कानूनी कार्रवाई दर्ज नहीं है।
hi.final_explanation:
यह समेकित प्रश्न विषय के प्रमुख विश्लेषणात्मक विषयों को एक साथ लाता है — Din-i-Ilahi की प्रकृति, इसकी विफलता, ulema का विरोध, और Akbar की नीतियों का दीर्घकालिक उलटफेर।

• कथन 1 — सही: Sulh-i-Kul/Din-i-Ilahi संबंध एक मौलिक भेद है। Sulh-i-Kul ब्रह्मांडीय-दार्शनिक आदर्श था; Din-i-Ilahi इसका न्यायालय स्तर पर संस्थागत रूप था जिसमें अनुष्ठान, सदस्यता और शिष्यत्व शामिल थे।
• कथन 2 — गलत: Jahangir ने Din-i-Ilahi सदस्यों पर कानूनी दंड नहीं लगाया। यह आदेश संस्थागत क्षय के कारण समाप्त हुआ — कोई करिश्माई गुरु नहीं था, कोई उत्तराधिकारी नहीं, कोई आधार नहीं। 'सक्रिय उत्पीड़न' एक निर्मित तथ्य है।
• कथन 3 — सही: तर्क महत्वपूर्ण है। यदि बाहरी विरोध (1580-81 की फतवा) ने Din-i-Ilahi को नष्ट किया होता, तो यह 1605 तक जीवित नहीं रहता। बाहरी विरोध के बावजूद इसका अस्तित्व और Akbar की मृत्यु पर पतन आंतरिक विफलता की पुष्टि करता है।
• कथन 4 — सही: Aurangzeb का 1679 में जिज्ञासा पुनः लागू करना Akbar की विरासत का सबसे तीव्र नीति उलटफेर है — 115 वर्षों के अंतराल के बाद पूर्व Akbari प्रथा की प्रतीकात्मक वापसी।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• कथन 3 में तर्क (बाहरी विरोध के बावजूद जीवित रहना → आंतरिक विफलता) प्रारंभिक परीक्षा के विश्लेषणात्मक तर्क के लिए आदर्श है।
• GS1 मुख्य परीक्षा के लिए: Din-i-Ilahi की विफलता के उत्तर को तीन कारणों पर आधारित करें — संरचनात्मक कमजोरी, संकीर्ण सामाजिक आधार, व्यक्तिगत करिश्मा पर निर्भरता।
• Akbar की व्यापक विरासत (जिज्ञासा उन्मूलन, राजपूत एकीकरण, समग्र संस्कृति) Din-i-Ilahi से अधिक टिकाऊ थी — यह आदेश उनके समन्वयात्मक प्रोजेक्ट का सबसे दृश्य लेकिन सबसे कम टिकाऊ हिस्सा था।
